entries.title: Library test: the Mudling (style key look)
entries.prompt:
IMAGE REQUEST: ONE SINGLE ILLUSTRATION. Return exactly one image.

The attached picture is the style key. Paint one new picture in exactly its painting style: the same dense painted texture, fine brushwork, deep saturated colors, warm lamplight and crisp detail.

A MUDLING, a small friendly mud monster, knee high: a rounded lump of brown mud with a puddle base, two stubby mud arms, big round shiny eyes, a small open mouth, and a little green sprout with two leaves on top of its head. It stands on a plain flat magenta background, full body, facing the viewer, a curious friendly look. No other characters, no text.

entries.title: Tom ability: Disconnected Controller (6 frames; needs your two battle sheets)
entries.prompt:
Draw the character in the attached pictures as one battle move sheet.

Picture 1 is the character. Picture 2 is their walk sheet. Pictures 3 and 4 are their battle sheets. Copy them as exactly as possible in every frame: the same person, face, age, body, head size compared to the body, hair, clothes, colors, painting style, level of detail, viewing angle and figure size as pictures 3 and 4. Only the pose, the object in the hands, and the front of the shirt change, as each frame says.

One image, a grid of 3 columns by 2 rows of equal square cells, on a flat solid magenta #FF00FF background. One figure per cell, the same size in every cell, feet on the same ground line, each figure well inside its cell. Held objects are painted in the same style as the character.

In every frame the character faces the same way as in pictures 3 and 4, in the same three-quarter view, unless a frame says he looks at the viewer.

The move: Disconnected Controller. The game controller printed on the front of his shirt pops off and becomes a real object in his hands. The controller he holds looks exactly like the one on his shirt in pictures 1 to 4: same shape, colors and details, now solid and three-dimensional. From frame 2 on, his shirt is plain navy with nothing on the front, and the rest of the shirt is unchanged.

Row 1:
1. Looking down at the controller on his shirt, tapping it twice with two fingers, calm curious face. The controller is still on the shirt.
2. The controller pops off the shirt and floats a hand's width in front of his chest. Both hands come up to catch it, eyebrows raised. His shirt is now plain navy.
3. Holding the controller in both hands at chest height, thumbs on the buttons, pressing one button hard, staring down at it, mouth flat.

Row 2:
4. Holding the controller out at arm's length in one hand, giving it a small shake, frowning at it, unimpressed.
5. Wind-up: the controller in one hand pulled back behind the shoulder, weight on the back leg, eyes narrowed.
6. Throw: the arm swung fully forward, the controller just leaving the open fingers, front knee bent, a dry satisfied look.

entries.title: Tom objects and effects: Disconnected Controller (7 items; attaches the approved Disconnected Controller sheet)
entries.prompt:
Paint the objects and effects for one battle move as one sheet.

The attached picture is the character's sheet for this move. Copy every object he holds in it exactly: the same shape, colors, details, size compared to his hands, painting style and light. Paint every new object and effect in that same painted style.

One image, a grid of 4 columns by 3 rows of equal square cells, on a flat solid magenta #FF00FF background. One item per cell, in the order of the list, filled row by row. Each item is centered, fills about 75 percent of its cell, and has clear magenta all around it; nothing touches a cell edge. Wide items fill the cell width, tall items fill the cell height. Cells with no item stay plain magenta.

No person, no hands, no body parts. No numbers, labels or captions. No words except lettering an item asks for.

Warm golden light from the upper left, soft painted shading, crisp clean edges, no thick black outlines, no cast shadow, no floor. Painted and realistic, not pixel art. Effects (splashes, glows, sparkles, smoke, ink, light) are painted as solid shapes with crisp edges, never faint haze, and never use magenta or pink.

The move: Disconnected Controller.

Items:
1. The game controller from the picture, front view.
2. The same controller tilted at an angle, as if spinning through the air.
3. A small no-signal badge: four rising signal bars with a red cross over them.
4. A curved white motion swoosh, the path of a thrown object (wide).
5. A big jagged impact burst, yellow and white.
6. Three plump golden stars in a small ring, for dizziness.
7. A small puff of grey dust.

entries.title: Tom emotion sheet: 8 feelings, full body (happy, loving, sad, angry, scared, surprised, proud, unimpressed)
entries.prompt:
Draw the character in the attached picture as an emotion sheet: the same person showing eight different feelings.

The attached picture is the character. Copy it as exactly as possible in every frame: the same person, face, age, body, head size compared to the body, hair, clothes, colors, painting style and level of detail. Only the pose and the face change.

One image, a grid of 4 columns by 2 rows of equal square cells, on a flat solid magenta #FF00FF background. One full-body figure per cell, from the top of the hair to the feet, standing, facing the viewer in a slight three-quarter view. The same figure size in every cell, feet on the same ground line, each figure well inside its cell. Empty hands. No grid lines, numbers, text, symbols, tears, sweat drops, hearts or effects. Each feeling must read from the whole body and from the face, clear enough to read at a small size.

Row 1:
1. Happy. Up on the toes, knees loose, a little bounce. Both hands clasped at chest height. Eyes crinkled, cheeks raised, a big open-mouth smile.
2. Loving. Feet together, head tilted to one side. Both hands pressed flat over the heart. Soft half-closed eyes, a warm closed-mouth smile.
3. Sad. Slumped, shoulders dropped, head lowered, feet together with the toes turned in. Hands holding each other in front of the waist. Eyebrows pulled up in the middle, the corners of the mouth turned down.
4. Angry. Feet planted wide, leaning forward, arms crossed tight over the chest. Chin down, eyebrows pulled down hard, eyes narrowed, a tight frown.

Row 2:
5. Scared. Knees bent, leaning back, shoulders hunched up. Both fists held up under the chin. Eyes wide open, eyebrows raised and pulled together, mouth open and stretched wide.
6. Surprised. One foot stepped back, upper body pulled back. Both hands open beside the face, palms forward. Eyebrows raised high, eyes wide and round, mouth open in a tall O.
7. Proud. Feet apart, chest out, shoulders back, chin raised. Both fists on the hips. A confident closed-mouth one-sided smile.
8. Unimpressed. Weight on one leg, the other knee relaxed. One hand on the hip, the other arm hanging loose. Head tilted, eyelids half lowered, one eyebrow raised, mouth a flat line pulled to one side.

entries.title: Library test: Mudling as a 2 x 2 grid, repainted over a soft underpainting
entries.prompt:
IMAGE REQUEST: ONE SINGLE ENEMY SHEET. Return exactly one image, nothing else.

WHAT THIS IS
The battle sheet of the enemy MUDLING (a regular enemy, level 1) for "The Adventures of Tom", a family role-playing game: 4 poses of the same character in a single row. The game puts it in front of a painted background of a sunlit pond ringed by reeds with big leafy trees, so its colors and handbrushed painted texture should feel at home there, painted in the same way as the area painting, but it must still stand out clearly against it.

ATTACHED IMAGES (in this order)
1. The STYLE KEY, a finished painting of the family in a school yard. This is the painting style to match exactly: dense, jewel-toned painted texture, fine visible brushwork, deep saturated colors, warm light.
2. The AREA PAINTING of a sunlit pond ringed by reeds with big leafy trees: the place Mudling lives and fights. Use it for the creature's world: its color palette, the color of its light and shadows, the dense handbrushed paint texture and the mood. Paint Mudling as a resident of this same picture, by the same hand: the warm key light stays at the upper left as described below, tinted by the area's light on its lit side, with the area's shadow colors in its shaded side, and its materials (moss, wood, brick, brass, glass, mud, cloth) painted brush stroke by brush stroke the way this painting paints them. Do not copy this painting's layout, buildings or props into the sheet.
3. A soft COLOR UNDERPAINTING of this whole sheet: the same 4 poses of Mudling, in the same order and in the same positions, blurred on purpose, like a painter's first block-in of color. It fixes each pose's shape, position, size, colors, face and expression, and nothing else. Paint the finished picture over it: repaint every pose in place, with the same layout, the same poses and the same character, and add the fine detail and brushwork the underpainting does not have, such as individual brush strokes, painted texture, highlights, crisp painterly edges and small painted details in the face and surfaces. The finished sheet is sharp, high resolution and richly detailed. Nothing from the underpainting is kept as it is: every edge, texture and highlight is freshly painted.

STYLE RULE (the most important instruction)
Every frame must look handbrushed and painted by the same hand as the attached paintings: dense painted texture, visible brush strokes that follow the form, layered paint, fine detail, deep saturated colors, crisp painterly edges. Every surface of the creature (skin, fur, moss, wood, metal, cloth, glass) is painted with brush strokes, never airbrushed smooth, never glossy plastic, never a 3D render. The creature is painted into the same world as the area painting, by the same hand, so a viewer cannot tell the creature and the area were painted by different artists.

ART STYLE
- A whimsical storybook illustration of a creature, painted by hand with real brushes in a rich, dense, jewel-toned style, exactly like the illustrated school-yard painting of the style key and the area painting. Up close it looks like an oil or gouache painting on canvas: visible individual brush strokes that follow the shape of every form, layered paint, fine painted texture, small hand-made variations of color from one stroke to the next, and a faint canvas grain. Gently simplified shapes. Friendly-scary, funny and full of personality, never grim. This is a game for a family with a 6 and a 9 year old.
- Warm golden light from the upper left, a soft warm glow, a gentle rim light, deep saturated colors with rich contrast and fine surface texture.
- Clean, crisp, painterly edges with fine detail, formed where one brush stroke meets the next. No thick or black outlines.
- NOT pixel art, NOT retro game art, NOT photorealistic, NOT a 3D render, NOT anime, NOT flat cartoon shading. No pixelation, no dithering, no limited color palette.

THE CREATURE
MUDLING: a squat dome of wet brown mud with one green sprout on its crown, two small bright eyes, a tiny open mouth and stubby dripping mud arms. It is about 16 inches tall (1.3 feet), measured from its base or feet to the top of its highest point. For comparison, the smallest enemy in the game, the Mudling, is 16 inches tall.

THE SHEET (strict)
- A single image holding a grid of 4 equal square cells, 2 columns by 2 rows, each cell 512 x 512 pixels, so the full image is 1024 x 1024 pixels. The layout is exactly the layout of the underpainting. If your tool cannot make that exact size, keep the same 2 by 2 grid and make the image as large as it allows.
- Exactly 4 frames, one per cell, in reading order (left to right along the top row, then left to right along the bottom row), in the numbered order below.
- MUDLING FACES RIGHT in every frame (toward the right side of the image), as if facing the family on the right of a battle screen. Seen from the side or three quarters, slightly from above.
- Background: one flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF filling the whole image. No magenta anywhere on the creature. No magenta glow, spill, tint or fringe on its edges. No grid lines, borders, cell backgrounds, numbers, labels, captions or titles.
- Same scale in every cell, exactly the scale and position of the figures in the underpainting, which already fills each cell as much as its widest pose allows. In every cell the feet or base rest on the same horizontal line as in the underpainting, with a small soft contact shadow directly under it. Nothing touches a cell edge or overlaps a neighbour.
- Draw ONLY MUDLING. No effects, motion lines, sparkles, other characters, props that are not part of it, text or word balloons.
- The same colors, details and level of painted detail in every frame.

THE 4 FRAMES
1. STANCE: battle stance, idle and ready, weight settled.
2. FLINCH: startled by a hit, recoiling a little, eyes shut or squinting.
3. ATTACK A: the wind-up for its signature attack, Mud Pie.
4. ATTACK B: the attack landing.

Family friendly for ages 6 and up. Keep the flinch frame comic, never grim.

NEVER substitute. Do not add extra frames, merge two frames or repeat a pose. If anything is unclear, draw MUDLING in the pose described, facing right, with the shape and colors of the likeness in attachment 3.

entries.prompt:
IMAGE REQUEST: ONE SINGLE ENEMY SHEET. Return exactly one image, nothing else. make sure it has a handbrushed painted look and feel

WHAT THIS IS
The battle sheet of the enemy MUDLING (a regular enemy, level 1) for "The Adventures of Tom", a family role-playing game: 4 poses of the same character in a single row. The game puts it in front of a painted background of a sunlit pond ringed by reeds with big leafy trees, so its colors and handbrushed painted texture should feel at home there, painted in the same way as the area painting, but it must still stand out clearly against it.

ATTACHED IMAGES (in this order)
1. The STYLE KEY, a finished painting of the family in a school yard. This is the painting style to match exactly: dense, jewel-toned painted texture, fine visible brushwork, deep saturated colors, warm light.
2. The AREA PAINTING of a sunlit pond ringed by reeds with big leafy trees: the place Mudling lives and fights. Use it for the creature's world: its color palette, the color of its light and shadows, the dense handbrushed paint texture and the mood. Paint Mudling as a resident of this same picture, by the same hand: the warm key light stays at the upper left as described below, tinted by the area's light on its lit side, with the area's shadow colors in its shaded side, and its materials (moss, wood, brick, brass, glass, mud, cloth) painted brush stroke by brush stroke the way this painting paints them. Do not copy this painting's layout, buildings or props into the sheet.
3. A LIKENESS picture of Mudling drawn in an older style. Use it for the creature's SHAPE, face, expression, colors and details ONLY. Do not copy how it is rendered: it is blocky and flat, and the new sheet must not be. Redraw Mudling from scratch, handbrushed and painted, keeping the same character.

STYLE RULE (the most important instruction)
Every frame must look handbrushed and painted by the same hand as the attached paintings: dense painted texture, visible brush strokes that follow the form, layered paint, fine detail, deep saturated colors, crisp painterly edges. Every surface of the creature (skin, fur, moss, wood, metal, cloth, glass) is painted with brush strokes, never airbrushed smooth, never glossy plastic, never a 3D render. The creature is painted into the same world as the area painting, by the same hand, so a viewer cannot tell the creature and the area were painted by different artists.

ART STYLE
- A whimsical storybook illustration of a creature, painted by hand with real brushes in a rich, dense, jewel-toned style, exactly like the illustrated school-yard painting of the style key and the area painting. Up close it looks like an oil or gouache painting on canvas: visible individual brush strokes that follow the shape of every form, layered paint, fine painted texture, small hand-made variations of color from one stroke to the next, and a faint canvas grain. Gently simplified shapes. Friendly-scary, funny and full of personality, never grim. This is a game for a family with a 6 and a 9 year old.
- Warm golden light from the upper left, a soft warm glow, a gentle rim light, deep saturated colors with rich contrast and fine surface texture.
- Clean, crisp, painterly edges with fine detail, formed where one brush stroke meets the next. No thick or black outlines.
- NOT pixel art, NOT retro game art, NOT photorealistic, NOT a 3D render, NOT anime, NOT flat cartoon shading. No pixelation, no dithering, no limited color palette.

MUDLING: a squat dome of wet brown mud with one green sprout on its crown, two small bright eyes, a tiny open mouth and stubby dripping mud arms. It is about 16 inches tall (1.3 feet), measured from its base or feet to the top of its highest point. For comparison, the smallest enemy in the game, the Mudling, is 16 inches tall.

- MUDLING FACES RIGHT in every frame (toward the right side of the image), as if facing the family on the right of a battle screen. Seen from the side or three quarters, slightly from above.
- Background: one flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF filling the whole image. No magenta anywhere on the creature. No magenta glow, spill, tint or fringe on its edges. No grid lines, borders, cell backgrounds, numbers, labels, captions or titles.

Its base or feet rest on one horizontal line about 16 pixels above the cell bottom, with a small soft contact shadow directly under it. Center each pose in its cell with at least 10 percent margin; nothing touches a cell edge or overlaps a neighbour.

THE 4 FRAMES
1. STANCE: battle stance, idle and ready, weight settled.
2. FLINCH: startled by a hit, recoiling a little, eyes shut or squinting.

A friendly small Long Island town square on a clear warm afternoon. Golden sunlight from the upper left, long soft shadows falling to the lower right, faint lilac light in the shade. Honey-cream cobblestone paving, mature leafy trees, low wooden fences, flower barrels and planters. Small-town coziness, not a palace or a city.

A character must be able to walk from any exit to every door and all the way around every building. No building, fence, tree or prop may wall off a route.

- North row: the alley between buildings 1 and 2 is the stone stairway lane that climbs to the TOP edge exit. The alleys between 2 and 3 and between 3 and 4 lead to a narrow cobbled garden path that runs BEHIND the whole north row, so you can circle every north building.
- South row: three wide alleys run straight DOWN from the plaza, between buildings 5 and 6, between 6 and 7, and between 7 and 8, to a cobbled lane that runs along the fronts of the south row. The alley between 6 and 7 is the widest and continues straight down to the BOTTOM edge exit.

ARCHITECTURE: EXACTLY EIGHT DISTINCT, STRONGLY THEMED BUILDINGS
Every building must be unmistakably its shop even with no sign: the theme is built into its shape, roofline, windows, trim and materials, not just props by the door. No two buildings share a silhouette. No generic cottages.
Four buildings along the NORTH side, left to right, doors facing the plaza below them:
1. Crumb Bakery (terracotta and golden crust-brown roof, honey walls): a plump rounded roof like a loaf of bread, a big brick bread-oven chimney puffing warm steam, a round oven-door window, iced-cake trim along the cornice, a striped awning over a window of bread and pastries, bread racks and flour sacks outside.

Penny's Pockets (coral-red roof, butter walls): an adventurer's outfitter and snack shop, backpacks, satchels, lanterns, rope and walking sticks hanging on the outside wall, a scalloped awning shaped like rows of pockets, a deep bay window of snack crates and candy jars, copper penny studs on the door, a pot of marigolds.

3. SPROUT / HOUSE: a leaf-shaped wooden board wrapped in vines, letters painted fresh green.

PLAZA
A wide paved plaza between the two rows. A LARGE round stone fountain, about one fifth of the image width, with a lower basin, a tiered spout and flowers around it, sits just left of the center with open paving all around it. Two wooden benches with flower barrels, one left and one right of the fountain. Iron street lamps along the plaza. Dense summer trees and wooden fences around the outer edges, leaving the three exits open.

LAYERING (the game cuts trees, lamps, signs and roofs out as separate layers)

LIGHT AND COLORS
Warm golden key light #FFE1A0, lilac accent in shade #C8A5DC, cream paving #EED8B5, leafy sage #608775, light green grass #B4C395, terracotta #CF7954, warm shadows #716351. Clear darker contact shadow under buildings and props, open sunlit plaza.

STRICT EXCLUSIONS
No people, no live animals, no monsters. No words, numbers or logos other than the eleven signs. No buildings touching each other. No grid, colored tiles, diamonds, numbered markers, map or diagram look. No pond, bridge, garden maze or water other than the fountain. No title card, frame, contact sheet or palette chart.

Jefferson Park, a Los Angeles neighborhood of 1910 craftsman bungalows, on a warm afternoon with purple jacaranda trees in bloom, a few palms and lawns. A row of small shops on Jefferson Boulevard and four homes on the street below. Warm, close-knit and a little crowded.

THIS IS A WALKABLE GAME MAP: NAVIGATION COMES FIRST
A character must be able to walk from every exit to every door and landmark and all the way around every building. No building, fence, tree or prop may wall off a route. Every path is at least two character-widths wide.

Odette's: yellow walls, purple roof, a big pot on the sign, a mural. La Ceiba: cream and blue, leaf sign, a roll-down grille. Board Room: pale blue with a skateboard mural and orange awning. Very Green Juice: white and green, leaf logo. Tom's House: a tidy greige craftsman with a gold front door and a small front porch. Jordan and Sam: a black modern flip with a white trim. Casa Alvarez: an orange craftsman with a teal door, laundry line, bikes and many chairs on the porch. Dakota and Ryan: a white modern flip with dark trim. Jacaranda and palm trees, a bus bench, mailboxes, street lamps, hedges, front-yard lemon trees.

House number plates: 3468 on Tom's house, 2732 on the black flip, ALVAREZ on the orange house, 2740 on the white flip. Exit boards: DOWNTOWN over the top road, OLD OAK PARK over the bottom road, CAR BARN over the east road.

Paving, ground and grass continue unbroken under and behind every tree, lamp, bench, sign post and roof eave. Every tall object has a clear visible base with ground showing behind it. Clearly separated, small-brush painted silhouettes on tree canopies, lamps, boards and roof edges. Nothing floats. The game cuts trees, lamps, boards and roofs out as separate layers.

Clear darker contact shadow under buildings and props, an open sunlit walkable center. Jacaranda purple #8A6AB0, stucco cream #F2E6D0, orange #D9A05A, teal #2F8A8A, lawn green #B4C395.

IMAGE REQUEST: ONE SINGLE ILLUSTRATION. Return exactly one image, nothing else.

WHAT THIS IS
A square interior painting of the Crumb Bakery, a cozy village bakery, for "The Adventures of Tom", a family role-playing game. It is one room, seen as a cutaway dollhouse view from above and in front, and the game places its characters on the floor.

ATTACHED IMAGES (in this order)
1. The installed painting of this same room: a LAYOUT AND FURNITURE reference. Keep the same furniture, the same placement and the same room layout, the same entrance position and the same wall and window positions. Restyle everything to attachment 2. Do not add rooms, do not remove furniture, do not move pieces to new walls.
2. The STYLE KEY, a finished painting of the family in a school yard. It shows exactly how this game paints: dense jewel-toned painted texture, fine brushwork, warm golden light. Match it. Take nothing else from it.

ART STYLE (the same look as attachment 2, the style key)
- Illustrated whimsical realism: a hand-painted interior with dense, jewel-toned painted texture, fine visible brushwork, deep saturated colors and rich contrast. Gently simplified shapes, crisp clean edges, fine surface detail on wood grain, fabric, plaster and stone. No thick or black outlines.
- Warm golden light from the upper left, a soft warm glow, a gentle rim light on furniture edges, soft baked contact shadows under every piece of furniture. Lamps and windows add small pools of warm light.

entries.title: 01 Pond Town: battle background (REPAINT, replaces bgs/01-pond-town.webp)
entries.prompt:
Paint one background picture for the battle screen of a family role-playing game: Pond Town (outdoor, daytime).

SCENE
A sunny afternoon at the pond at the edge of a small Long Island town, painted as a wide calm landscape. Across the full width a band of still blue-green pond water fills y 400 to y 565, with soft sky reflections. On the far shore: a tiny village, a white church with a steeple (center-right, steeple tip near y 290), three or four cottages with red and grey roofs, and a line of oaks and dark green evergreens. Two big leafy oak trees frame the far left and far right edges, trunk bases at about y 560, canopies reaching the top edge. The near bank is a soft grassy strip that ends exactly on the horizon line at y 590, with a few reed and cattail tufts allowed only above y 575. A small wooden dock reaches into the water at right of center, entirely above y 590. Sky: clear soft blue with a few big, gentle cumulus clouds, sun high at the upper left.

THE FLOOR (everything below y 590)
Flat packed dirt with a dusting of short dry grass, warm sand-tan (about #B3A27C) with a faint olive-green tone. Even in tone from left to right. No ruts, stones, puddles, tufts or water edge below y 590.

entries.title: Library test: Pond Grump as a 2 x 2 grid, matte and handbrushed finish copied from an approved picture
entries.prompt:
IMAGE REQUEST: ONE SINGLE ENEMY SHEET. Return exactly one image, nothing else.

WHAT THIS IS
The battle sheet of the enemy POND GRUMP (a regular enemy, level 1) for "The Adventures of Tom", a family role-playing game: 4 poses of the same character in a single row. The game puts it in front of a painted background of a sunlit pond ringed by reeds with big leafy trees, so its colors and handbrushed painted texture should feel at home there, painted in the same way as the area painting, but it must still stand out clearly against it.

ATTACHED IMAGES (in this order)
1. The STYLE KEY, a finished painting of the family in a school yard. This is the painting style to match exactly: dense, jewel-toned painted texture, fine visible brushwork, deep saturated colors, warm light.
2. The AREA PAINTING of a sunlit pond ringed by reeds with big leafy trees: the place Pond Grump lives and fights. Use it for the creature's world: its color palette, the color of its light and shadows, the dense handbrushed paint texture and the mood. Paint Pond Grump as a resident of this same picture, by the same hand: the warm key light stays at the upper left as described below, tinted by the area's light on its lit side, with the area's shadow colors in its shaded side, and its materials (moss, wood, brick, brass, glass, mud, cloth) painted brush stroke by brush stroke the way this painting paints them. Do not copy this painting's layout, buildings or props into the sheet.
3. A soft COLOR UNDERPAINTING of this whole sheet: the same 4 poses of Pond Grump, in the same order and in the same positions, blurred on purpose, like a painter's first block-in of color. It fixes each pose's shape, position, size, colors, face and expression, and nothing else. Paint the finished picture over it: repaint every pose in place, with the same layout, the same poses and the same character, and add the fine detail and brushwork the underpainting does not have, such as individual brush strokes, painted texture, highlights, crisp painterly edges and small painted details in the face and surfaces. The finished sheet is sharp, high resolution and richly detailed. Nothing from the underpainting is kept as it is: every edge, texture and highlight is freshly painted.
4. A FINISHED picture of a different creature, painted in exactly the surface finish wanted for this sheet: matte, with visible brush strokes, ridges of paint, layered color and a canvas grain. Use it ONLY for how the paint looks (the matte finish, the brushwork, the sharpness of the edges). Do not copy its creature, pose or layout: the creature, poses and layout come only from attachment 3.

STYLE RULE (the most important instruction)
Every frame must look handbrushed and painted by the same hand as the attached paintings: dense painted texture, visible brush strokes that follow the form, layered paint, fine detail, deep saturated colors, crisp painterly edges. Every surface of the creature (skin, fur, moss, wood, metal, cloth, glass) is painted with brush strokes, never airbrushed smooth, never glossy plastic, never a 3D render. The creature is painted into the same world as the area painting, by the same hand, so a viewer cannot tell the creature and the area were painted by different artists.

SURFACE AND BRUSHWORK (the most important instruction)
Every surface is matte, like dry oil paint or gouache on canvas. Light is shown by broad, soft highlights built from visible brush strokes with dry-brush texture along their edges. Brush strokes are clearly visible everywhere and vary in size: broad strokes for the large forms, short flicks for texture, thick ridges of paint on the lit side of every form. Color is built in layers, so warm and cool tones show through each other. Edges are painted crisp with a small brush. A fine canvas weave grain lies over the whole picture. NOT glossy, NOT wet-looking, NOT plastic, NOT airbrushed, NOT a 3D render.

ART STYLE
- A whimsical storybook illustration of a creature, painted by hand with real brushes in a rich, dense, jewel-toned style, exactly like the illustrated school-yard painting of the style key and the area painting. Up close it looks like an oil or gouache painting on canvas: visible individual brush strokes that follow the shape of every form, layered paint, fine painted texture, small hand-made variations of color from one stroke to the next, and a faint canvas grain. Gently simplified shapes. Friendly-scary, funny and full of personality, never grim. This is a game for a family with a 6 and a 9 year old.
- Warm golden light from the upper left, a soft warm glow, a gentle rim light, deep saturated colors with rich contrast and fine surface texture.
- Clean, crisp, painterly edges with fine detail, formed where one brush stroke meets the next. No thick or black outlines.
- NOT pixel art, NOT retro game art, NOT photorealistic, NOT a 3D render, NOT anime, NOT flat cartoon shading. No pixelation, no dithering, no limited color palette.

THE CREATURE
POND GRUMP: a fat round-shouldered mossy olive-green toad lump with a pale sagging belly, pondweed hanging like wet hair and a permanent scowl. It is about 24 inches tall (2 feet), measured from its base or feet to the top of its highest point. For comparison, the smallest enemy in the game, the Mudling, is 16 inches tall.

THE SHEET (strict)
- A single image holding a grid of 4 equal square cells, 2 columns by 2 rows, each cell 512 x 512 pixels, so the full image is 1024 x 1024 pixels. The layout is exactly the layout of the underpainting. If your tool cannot make that exact size, keep the same 2 by 2 grid and make the image as large as it allows.
- Exactly 4 frames, one per cell, in reading order (left to right along the top row, then left to right along the bottom row), in the numbered order below.
- POND GRUMP FACES RIGHT in every frame (toward the right side of the image), as if facing the family on the right of a battle screen. Seen from the side or three quarters, slightly from above.
- Background: one flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF filling the whole image. No magenta anywhere on the creature. No magenta glow, spill, tint or fringe on its edges. No grid lines, borders, cell backgrounds, numbers, labels, captions or titles.
- Same scale in every cell, exactly the scale and position of the figures in the underpainting, which already fills each cell as much as its widest pose allows. In every cell the feet or base rest on the same horizontal line as in the underpainting, with a small soft contact shadow directly under it. Nothing touches a cell edge or overlaps a neighbour.
- Draw ONLY POND GRUMP. No effects, motion lines, sparkles, other characters, props that are not part of it, text or word balloons.
- The same colors, details and level of painted detail in every frame.

THE 4 FRAMES
1. STANCE: battle stance, idle and ready, weight settled.
2. FLINCH: startled by a hit, recoiling a little, eyes shut or squinting.
3. ATTACK A: the wind-up for its signature attack, Soggy Slap.
4. ATTACK B: the attack landing.

Family friendly for ages 6 and up. Keep the flinch frame comic, never grim.

NEVER substitute. Do not add extra frames, merge two frames or repeat a pose. If anything is unclear, draw POND GRUMP in the pose described, facing right, with the shape and colors of the likeness in attachment 3.

entries.title: Trail clues, chapters 1 to 3 (9 objects)
entries.prompt:
IMAGE REQUEST: ONE SINGLE PROP SHEET. Return exactly one image, nothing else. Follow the numbered list at the bottom exactly.

WHAT THIS IS
A sheet of find-it objects for "The Adventures of Tom", a family role-playing game. This is the sheet for trails for chapters 1 to 3: it holds 9 trail clue objects that lead the player, one after another, toward a hidden enemy or boss. Each group of three is in trail order, from the faintest clue to the strongest. They will be cut out and drawn on top of a painted dungeon map, so each one must stand out clearly from a painted background.

ATTACHED IMAGES (in this order)
1. The STYLE KEY, a finished painting of the family in a school yard. Match how it paints: dense painted texture, fine visible brushwork, deep saturated colors, warm light. Do not copy any person, building or scene from it. Paint only the objects listed below.

ART STYLE
- Every object is painted by hand in the style of the attached style key: dense painted texture, fine visible brushwork, deep saturated jewel colors, crisp clean edges, clear readable shapes. Gently simplified, storybook-like shapes.
- Warm golden key light from the upper left. Shadow on the lower right of each form, and at most a tiny soft contact shadow under each object, no cast shadow on a floor, no ground plane.
- No thick or black outlines.
- NOT pixel art, NOT retro game art, NOT photorealistic, NOT a 3D render, NOT anime, NOT flat cartoon shading. No pixelation, no dithering, no limited color palette, no glossy plastic look.
- Make each object read at a glance: slightly more saturated and a little higher contrast than a normal background object, and give the part the player touches (a switch, a lock, a slot, a handle) the brightest accent color on the object.
- Three-quarter view from slightly above, unless the list says "seen from the front". All objects share one lighting direction and one level of detail. Fun, friendly, a little silly. Family friendly for children aged 6 and up.

THE SHEET (strict)
- A grid of 4 columns by 4 rows of square cells, 256 x 256 pixels each, so the full image is 1024 x 1024 pixels. If your tool offers a different size, keep exactly 4 columns and 4 rows and use the largest size available.
- Exactly 9 objects, one per cell, filled left to right, top to bottom, in the order of the numbered list below. The final cells (numbers 10 to 16) must stay completely empty and transparent, with no number.
- Each object is drawn complete, centered in its own cell, fully inside it, with at least 12 percent empty margin on every side. Nothing touches or crosses a cell edge. Nothing overlaps a neighbouring cell.
- Scale every object to fill about 70 to 80 percent of its cell, regardless of its real-world size. Small things are enlarged to the same footprint.
- Background: fully transparent (PNG with alpha). No grid lines, no borders, no frames, no cell backgrounds, no checkerboard pattern. If your tool cannot output transparency, fill the entire background with one flat solid color, pure magenta #FF00FF, and use no magenta anywhere inside the objects.
- In the top-left corner of every filled cell, put a small plain white number (with a thin dark outline) matching the list number. These numbers are a guide only and will be cropped off. Do not put any other labels, captions or titles on the sheet. The only text allowed is the text that is part of the object itself, spelled exactly as given in the list.

HARD RULES
- THE LIST IS COMPLETE AND DELIBERATE. Draw exactly the 9 objects described, one per numbered cell. NEVER substitute, swap in or add other objects, even ones that seem more typical, more common or related to the same theme. If a description is unusual, draw it as written. Every cell must match its numbered description.
- Where the list says "the same as cell N" or "identical to cell N", the object must match that cell exactly in shape, size and the position of every part, and only the change the list names may differ. These pairs are swapped in the game when something happens, so they must line up.
- Objects only. No people, no characters, no hands, no faces on anything unless the list says the object has a face. No creatures except the ones listed.
- No real brands, logos, trademarks or copyrighted characters.
- Do not add extra objects, decorations, sparkle bursts, motion lines, glows, smoke or effects beyond what the list describes. Small details the list names (a wisp of steam, a drip, a glint) are fine.
- Do not skip, merge or reorder any item.

THE 9 OBJECTS (cell number: name, what to draw)
1. CH1 CRUMB 1, SMALL: Three tiny golden pastry crumbs and one flaky crust flake with a dusting of cinnamon sugar, lying together in a loose little pile. The smallest, quietest clue of the trail.
2. CH1 CRUMB 2, TRAIL: A longer scattered line of golden rhubarb crisp crumbs with one sticky pink rhubarb smear and one half crumbled oat cluster, pointing to the right.
3. CH1 CRUMB 3, BITE: A big broken wedge of rhubarb crisp with a huge bite taken out of it, spilling crumbs and pink filling, with one wide toothy bite mark clearly visible.
4. CH2 TAR CLUE 1, DRIP: A small shiny black tar puddle with three round drips splashed beside it and one bubble on the surface, a faint curl of grey smoke rising from it.
5. CH2 TAR CLUE 2, FOOTPRINT: A pair of huge sticky black footprints pressed into a patch of cracked dusty ground, the toes spread wide, thick tar strings stretching up from the heel.
6. CH2 TAR CLUE 3, CRACK: A jagged crack in a square of pale cracked ground, dark fumes seeping out of it, little pebbles bouncing on the edge as if something is rumbling below.
7. CH3 WET CLUE 1, DRIP LINE: Three big glistening water drops on a flat dark green leaf, in a row getting larger from left to right, with one tiny tadpole shaped splash mark beside them.
8. CH3 WET CLUE 2, SCALE: One large overlapping teal armored fish scale with a bright wet shine, half stuck in a little puddle of muddy water, with a swirl of ripples around it.
9. CH3 WET CLUE 3, CLAW MARKS: Four long deep curved claw gouges scratched across a flat round piece of grey stone, with a few chips of stone and a thin trickle of water running out of the grooves.

entries.title: Tom, Grace and Rose: greeting hug on arrival in Long Island (8 frames)
entries.prompt:
Draw the man and the two little girls in the attached pictures as a greeting sheet.

Attached first: the man. Attached second: the older girl. Attached third: the younger girl. Copy all three pictures as exactly as possible in every frame: the same faces, bodies, head sizes compared to their bodies, hair, clothes, colors, linework, painting style and level of detail. Keep their real size difference the same in every frame: the man is tallest, the older girl is shorter, the younger girl is the smallest. Only the poses change. Do not add, remove or redesign anything.

One image, a grid of 4 columns by 2 rows of equal square cells, on a flat solid magenta #FF00FF background. The same figure scale in every cell, the man's feet on the same ground line, nothing touching a cell edge. Pink clothing stays clearly pink, never magenta. Hands empty. No grid lines, numbers, text, hearts, effects or shadows.

In every frame all of them face the viewer, in a slight three-quarter view. The mood is sweet, warm and family friendly.

Row 1 (the man alone, then the girls arrive):
1. Hearing them. The man stands alone, relaxed, head turned a little to one side, eyebrows lifting, eyes widening, a small surprised smile starting.
2. Delighted. The man alone, standing, a huge happy smile, eyes bright, both arms starting to open outward at his sides.
3. Crouching. The man alone, crouched low on both feet, knees bent wide, both arms open wide and low, a big loving grin, ready to be hugged.
4. Running in. The man crouched with arms open. The older girl runs in toward him from one side and the younger girl runs in from the other side, both with arms stretched out, mouths open in happy shouts, the younger girl hopping, both a step away from him.

Row 2 (the hug):
5. Crash. The two girls have just reached him, one on each side, arms flung around his neck and shoulders. The man is still crouched, his arms closing around both of them, eyes squeezed shut, mouth open in a happy laugh.
6. Group hug. The man crouched, one arm around each girl, holding them close. The older girl's cheek is pressed against his cheek, the younger girl's head tucked under his chin. All three have eyes closed and warm smiles.
7. Squeeze. The man crouched, hugging both tight, rocking slightly. The younger girl's feet are just off the ground, the older girl squeezing his neck. All three laughing with eyes crinkled.
8. Looking up. Still crouched in a loose hug, the man's hands resting on the girls' backs, all three smiling and looking at each other, content and happy.

Only the pose and the expression change.

In EVERY frame Michael carries both children against his chest, one on each forearm, exactly as in picture 1: each child sits on his bent forearm with his hand holding their back. Their faces are fully visible and friendly. His arms never let go. A frame with empty arms, a child on the ground, a child on his shoulders, or a missing child is WRONG. Michael is 6 feet 4 inches, the tallest adult.

In every frame he faces the same way as the profile row of picture 2, in the same three-quarter view, unless a frame says he turns to the viewer. His arms stay holding the children; only his body, head and legs act.

The move: MICHAEL ANSWERS.

Row 1:
1. Standing still, head turned toward a faraway shout, eyebrows lifted, a flat, caught-off-guard look, both children looking the same way.
2. Calling back over his shoulder, mouth open mid-shout, body leaning toward the voice, both children bouncing on his arms.

4. Winding up: body twisted away from the target, weight on the back leg, one shoulder cocked back, chin tucked, eyes narrowed, both children held snug against his chest.
5. The heave: a big forward step, front knee bent, the cocked shoulder driving forward, mouth open in a shout, both children held tight and wide-eyed.
